name: Universidad CEU San Pablo
summary: Private university in Madrid; 15 bachelor's with a confirmed English route, from dentistry and physiotherapy to data science and design.

ib.text: Apply with your grades, a motivation letter and ID, then interview. IB holders need the UNEDasiss credential to enrol. English-track students certify B2 English by the end of year 2.

programmes.name: Business Administration and Management
programmes.about: Business administration with two specialisation tracks in years 3 and 4, offered in an English group, with one or two semesters abroad possible.
programmes.overview: The first two years build the foundations: business management, microeconomics and macroeconomics, accounting, mathematics, statistics and marketing, followed by financial analysis, operations and business taxation. Teaching is practical, with Bloomberg terminals in the classroom, data-analysis software, and companies that co-teach selected subjects. In the final year you choose one of six pathways (economics, business law, business intelligence, business management, finance and accounting, or marketing), complete a compulsory internship and write a final project. Graduates go into financial analysis, consulting, operations, HR and strategy roles, or start their own ventures.
programmes.selectionNote: Decided on your grades, a motivation letter and an interview with a lecturer; online tests (English, maths for some) may follow.

programmes.name: Business Administration and Management + Marketing
programmes.about: Two degrees in five years, business administration and marketing, which you can study in English.
programmes.overview: This five-year route pairs a full business administration programme with marketing, starting from microeconomics, accounting, mathematics and company law, then moving into consumer behaviour, market research, pricing, product development, and digital and international marketing. You learn through group work, marketing simulators and workshops with industry professionals, and companies take part as co-teachers in some subjects. The last year brings a compulsory internship, a final thesis and electives such as e-commerce or sustainability, and exchange semesters at partner universities abroad are possible. Graduates work as marketing or product managers, business and financial analysts, consultants or entrepreneurs.

programmes.name: Computer Engineering
programmes.about: Programming, cybersecurity, systems, databases and software at CEU's Institute of Technology, with 40 places in the English group.
programmes.overview: The degree runs from programming, mathematics and physics in the first year through computer architecture, databases, networks and operating systems, to artificial intelligence, software engineering and enterprise information systems, and finally cybersecurity, web systems and business management. Small practical groups and laboratories, including a FabLab and virtual reality equipment, carry much of the teaching, and a compulsory internship and a final degree project close the course. A cybersecurity diploma can be added in years three and four. Graduates become software developers, systems analysts, IT security engineers, project managers or technology consultants.
programmes.selectionNote: Decided on your grades, a motivation letter and an interview with a lecturer; online tests (English, maths for some) may follow.

programmes.name: Data Science and Engineering
programmes.about: Data science and engineering in a 100%-English group of 30 places (a separate Spanish group also runs).
programmes.overview: Mathematics, statistics and computer science are the base, moving from programming, databases and computer architecture in the first year to machine learning, big data, deep learning, optimisation and robotics in years two and three. Coursework is built around real projects and lab work with high-performance computing and cloud resources, with team problem solving supervised by experts from industry. In the later years you pick bioinformatics, business information systems or an open mix of electives, and finish with an internship and a final project. Graduates work as data scientists, data engineers, data architects, big data developers or AI systems designers.
programmes.selectionNote: Decided on your grades, a motivation letter and an interview with a lecturer; online tests (English, maths for some) may follow.

programmes.name: Data Science and Data Engineering + Information Systems Engineering
programmes.about: Two engineering degrees in five years, taught in English, with tracks such as bioinformatics and business information systems.
programmes.overview: Two engineering degrees are combined, so the early years cover mathematics, statistics, physics and programming, then machine learning, cloud infrastructure, neural networks, databases and software engineering, and later Bayesian analysis, distributed computing and the management of information systems. Real-world projects supervised by industry experts run through the course, along with labs for high-performance computing, virtual reality and data analysis, and a compulsory internship in the fourth year. You complete the business information systems track and can add bioinformatics or open electives. Graduates work as data scientists, data engineers, software engineers, security engineers, IT directors or consultants.

programmes.name: Dentistry
programmes.about: A five-year dentistry degree that you can study entirely in English, with clinical training at CEU's Faculty of Medicine.
programmes.overview: The five years move from biology, anatomy, physiology, biochemistry and psychology into microbiology, pharmacology, biomaterials and head and neck anatomy, then paediatric dentistry, oral pathology, orthodontics, prosthetics and surgery, and finally periodontics, implantology, endodontics and maxillofacial surgery. Clinical training is central: students practise first in a simulation hospital and on a university polyclinic, and from the third year treat real patients under supervision. Electives include practice management and oral microbiota. Graduates work in private practice or hospital dentistry, research, teaching and public health.
programmes.selectionNote: Decided on your grades, a motivation letter and an interview with a lecturer; online tests (English, maths for some) may follow.

programmes.name: Physiotherapy
programmes.about: Physiotherapy at CEU's Faculty of Medicine, offered entirely in English as well as in Spanish.
programmes.overview: Anatomy, biology, physiology and biomechanics lead into pathology, manual therapy and musculoskeletal physiotherapy, then neurology, cardiorespiratory care, paediatrics and research methods. Most of the training is practical: simulated treatment rooms and a clinical simulation hospital come first, a university polyclinic offers real-patient practice, and external hospital and clinic placements begin in the second year. The final year has intensive clinical rotations and a capstone project, and electives include sports physiotherapy and intensive care. Graduates work in hospitals, primary care, sports clubs, specialist centres, research or their own practice.
programmes.selectionNote: Decided on your grades, a motivation letter and an interview with a lecturer; online tests (English, maths for some) may follow.

programmes.name: International Relations and the European Union
programmes.about: International relations and EU studies taught in English at the Law School, with cases, simulations and debates, and an option to add a second degree.
programmes.overview: You study geopolitics, the theory and history of international relations, international public law, the history and institutions of the European Union, and diplomacy and negotiation, together with a modern language. Later years add EU law, human rights, the single market, international trade and regional studies, with electives such as migration and asylum, and a final dissertation. Teaching uses case resolution, simulations and debates, and one semester abroad is compulsory. A second degree in law, economics or journalism can be added. Graduates go into European institutions, diplomacy, NGOs, journalism, consulting and international departments of companies.
programmes.selectionNote: Decided on your grades, a motivation letter and an interview with a lecturer; online tests (English, maths for some) may follow.

programmes.name: Advertising and Public Relations
programmes.ib: English track taught in English except the Spanish language course, the final project and internships.
programmes.about: A practical, multidisciplinary advertising and PR degree that you can take entirely in English apart from a few components.
programmes.overview: The first years cover writing, art and design, photography, advertising principles and communication theory, then creative thinking, public relations techniques, radio, video and digital production. Third year turns to advertising creativity, brand management and research methods, and the last year brings an internship, a final project and electives such as campaign planning or corporate reputation. Students work in the HUB, a communication and advertising agency run inside the school, and use TV and radio studios, photography labs and editing suites. Graduates become creative directors, account executives, copywriters, community managers and brand managers.
programmes.selectionNote: Decided on your grades, a motivation letter and an interview with a lecturer; online tests (English, maths for some) may follow.

programmes.name: Audiovisual Communication
programmes.ib: English track taught in English except the Spanish language course, the final project and internships.
programmes.about: Audiovisual communication with an international profile, available in English apart from a few components.
programmes.overview: The first year mixes contemporary history, art and design, photography, writing and communication theory; later years move to radio and podcast production, television and video, audiovisual narrative, cinematography, screenwriting and editing. The final year adds digital composition, sound and multi-camera production, an internship with media or production companies, and a final project. Students work on content projects in an in-house agency called the HUB and use television and radio studios, post-production rooms and photography labs from the start. Graduates work as producers, directors, scriptwriters and editors in television, radio and film, or in corporate communication and press offices.
programmes.selectionNote: Decided on your grades, a motivation letter and an interview with a lecturer; online tests (English, maths for some) may follow.

programmes.name: Digital Communication
programmes.about: Digital communication including virtual reality, gamification and interactive environments, with an English option.
programmes.overview: After a first year of photography, writing, communication theory and the basics of advertising, the course adds graphic communication, web programming, radio, podcasts and television, then social media management, brand reputation, strategic communication and data analytics. Teaching is learning by doing, in a student-run space called the HUB and in editing suites, TV and radio studios and photography labs, with free loan of cameras and recorders. Electives cover virtual and augmented reality, gamification and transmedia storytelling, and the last year has an external internship and a final project. Graduates work as social media, community or brand managers, UX designers, content creators and digital marketers.
programmes.selectionNote: Decided on your grades, a motivation letter and an interview with a lecturer; online tests (English, maths for some) may follow.

programmes.name: Journalism
programmes.ib: CEU says the English track is taught almost entirely in English.
programmes.about: Journalism that CEU offers almost entirely in English, with exchanges with universities in 25 countries.
programmes.overview: Writing, photography, communication theory and contemporary history open the course, followed by radio and podcast production, television and video, journalistic editing and documentation, then audiovisual journalism, ethics, communication law, data visualisation and international relations. Students train by doing, using two TV studios, two radio studios and editing rooms, and publishing through the school's HUB platform. An external internship at a Spanish media outlet and a final project come in the fourth year, with elective strands in sports, political and economic, cultural and scientific, or socio-religious journalism. Graduates work as journalists and editors, community managers, press officers and photojournalists.
programmes.selectionNote: Decided on your grades, a motivation letter and an interview with a lecturer; online tests (English, maths for some) may follow.

programmes.name: Fundamentals of Architecture
programmes.about: The new architecture bachelor's, with 100%-English or 100%-Spanish training; design, sustainability and urban planning.
programmes.overview: You start with drawing, geometry, materials, form analysis and structures, then move into design studios, building construction, urban design, structural analysis and environmental and electrical systems. Teaching is studio-based and project-driven, with workshops that mimic professional practice from the first year, and an optional internship at architecture practices. The final years add advanced design projects and construction detailing, with a choice between a Building Design mention and a Building Technology mention, and a final thesis. Graduates go into independent practice, urban planning, heritage restoration, construction management, BIM, sustainability consulting or research.
programmes.selectionNote: Decided on your grades, a motivation letter and an interview with a lecturer; online tests (English, maths for some) may follow.

programmes.name: Interior Design
programmes.about: Four years creating and rehabilitating interior spaces, with an English group of 40 places.
programmes.overview: The first year covers drawing, design basics, representation systems, light and colour and computer-assisted drawing; later years add design studios, construction materials and systems, retail and domestic design, public spaces, lighting and electrical design and refurbishment techniques. In year four come digital fabrication, scenography, furniture, garden and landscape design, exhibition design, project management and a final project. Learning is project-based, with 3D modelling and rendering, a FabLab, model workshops and a virtual reality lab, plus a mandatory professional internship. Graduates work as interior designers, project managers, design directors and retail consultants in studios and architecture firms.
programmes.selectionNote: Decided on your grades, a motivation letter and an interview with a lecturer; online tests (English, maths for some) may follow.

programmes.name: Fashion Design and Management and its Industry
programmes.about: Creating, leading and positioning fashion brands, with an English group of 30 places at CEU's creativity campus.
programmes.overview: The first year brings design basics, textiles, fashion sociology, pattern making, art history, marketing and management economics, and later years add brand identity, digital design tools, product design, communication strategy, business strategy and sustainability. Four project workshops build from creative experiments to a full collection, and teaching takes place in design studios, animation studios and innovation labs on a creativity campus, with links to fashion companies, shows and fairs. A mandatory external internship and a degree project close the course. Graduates work as fashion designers, product managers, creative directors, trend consultants, brand managers and merchandisers, or start their own labels.
programmes.selectionNote: Decided on your grades, a motivation letter and an interview with a lecturer; online tests (English, maths for some) may follow.

notes: Most degrees run a Spanish and an English group; the English group costs more per credit, and the fees shown are the 2026/27 English prices.
Admitted students pay a €950 place reservation fee (€1,500 for Dentistry) and a €1,500–2,000 enrolment fee.
Financial Markets and Data Analysis, taught in English, is listed as coming soon and is not included here.
